title: 27.37 · Lift-off of a conducting bar
given: Bar L = 0.500 m, mass 0.750 kg, B = 0.450 T into the page; current runs rightward. Series resistance starts at 25.0 Ω, then falls to 2.0 Ω.
find: Find maximum battery voltage before lift-off, then initial acceleration after resistance falls.

steps.title: Part (a): balance the weight at lift-off

answer: Maximum ≈ 817 V; initial acceleration ≈ 113 m/s² upward.
check: This is the initial acceleration while current still flows through the contacts; the circuit breaks when the bar lifts off.

title: 27.41 · Torque about a loop hinge
given: Rectangle abcd: vertical ab = cd = 0.200 m; horizontal bc = da = 0.350 m. Clockwise current 5.00 A; B = 1.20 T rightward; hinge along left side ab.
find: Find force directions, identify which force torques the hinge, and calculate torque.
answer: Only cd torques the hinge: 1.20 N outward; torque 0.420 N m.
note: Force on ab is into the page; force on cd is out of the page. The other two sides are parallel to B.
check: The right side cd swings out of the page. Net force is zero, but the force couple produces nonzero torque.

title: 27.42 · Rotating a current loop
given: Loop 0.220 m × 0.350 m, I = 1.95 A counterclockwise, B = 1.50 T into page. Initially loop plane is perpendicular to B; then rotate 30° with left side outward and right side inward.
find: Find net force and torque before and after rotation.
answer: Both net forces zero; torque 0 initially, then 0.113 N m continuing the rotation.
check: The initial magnetic moment is opposite B (unstable equilibrium). After the stated rotation the torque continues that rotation, with left side moving further out.

title: 27.56 · Cyclotron energy limit
given: Cyclotron B = 0.85 T, maximum orbit radius 0.40 m. Proton q = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. Alpha q = 3.20 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 6.64 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.
find: Find proton maximum energy in J/eV, period, B needed to double energy, and alpha maximum energy at 0.85 T.
answer: Proton 5.54 MeV; period 77.2 ns; doubling requires 1.20 T; alpha 5.57 MeV.
check: The alpha energy is almost the same: its charge squared is four times greater and mass approximately four times greater. Nonrelativistic model.

title: 27.65 · Rail-gun acceleration
given: A bar of mass m and length L bridges horizontal rails in uniform vertical field B, carrying constant current I across the bar as shown in the handout. Ignore friction and gravity for the motion.
find: Derive force and distance from rest to speed v; evaluate for 11.2 km/s, B = 0.80 T, I = 2.0 × 10³ A, m = 25 kg, L = 0.50 m.
answer: F = ILB along rails; d = mv²/(2ILB); example distance 1.96 × 10⁶ m.
check: Force points along the rails away from the source for the shown current. The 1960 km distance illustrates the limits of this simplified launch model.

title: 27.69 · Suspended loop in equilibrium
given: Loop width 6.00 cm, height 8.00 cm, mass per length 0.15 g/cm, current 8.2 A as in handout. Hinge is its upper 6 cm side; plane tilts 30° from yz-plane. B is parallel to y.
find: Find magnitude and direction of B needed for equilibrium.

steps.title: Find loop mass and gravity torque
